M_R is the R-span of M inside V: its elements are finite sums of r m with r in R and m in M. The natural multiplication map R tensor_Z M -> V sends r tensor m to r m. The definition by the image does not assume injectivity of this map.
For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique complex-linear operator with E_ij e_j=e_i and E_ij e_k=0 for every k in I different from j, extended linearly using the complex basis e.
Pi=Y_lambda X_lambda; juxtaposition of operators means composition with the rightmost operator applied first.
J={c in C : c v belongs to M_R}. No generator of J is selected in this definition.

definitions.definition: For a complex-linear T with T(M) subset M, red(T) is induced by its integer-linear restriction to M: red(T)(m tensor c)=T(m) tensor c for m in M and c in K, extended K-linearly. This is the tensor extension of an integer-linear map. Expressions red(T) are used only after T(M) subset M is established. The reduced generators in the target are red(x), red(y), red(h).

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0 <= lambda < p.

n=lambda+1>0, I has n elements, dim_C V=n, and (e_i)_{i in I} is a complex basis of V, with e_0=v. For every integer t>=0, h y^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v; for t>=1, x y^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^{t-1}v. All y^t v vanish for t>lambda. The matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1<=i<=lambda, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0<=i<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i. For every i in I and r>=0, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r<=i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these divided-power coefficients are integers.

Multiplication R tensor_Z M -> V, s tensor m -> s m, is injective with image M_R. M_R is free over R of rank n and spans V over C. Every X_r and Y_r (r>=0) preserves M and M_R; x,y,h preserve M and M_R, so their reductions are defined. For all i,j in I, Pi=E_{lambda,lambda}, X_{lambda-i} Pi=E_{i,lambda}, Pi Y_{lambda-j}=binom(lambda,j) E_{lambda,j}, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R, and E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_{lambda-i} Pi Y_{lambda-j}. Consequently every E_ij preserves M_R.

For each i in I the R-module {c in C : c e_i in M_R} equals J. The R-module J is finitely generated and nonzero. The map J^I -> M_R taking (c_i) to sum_{i in I} c_i e_i is an R-linear isomorphism, with inverse the tuple of complex coordinates in the basis e; in particular M_R is the internal direct sum of the modules J e_i.

inputs.statement: Let A be a commutative semiring, S a multiplicative submonoid of A, B a commutative semiring and A-algebra which is a localization of A at S, and T an additive commutative monoid with A-module structure. Then f:T -> B tensor_A T, f(t)=1 tensor t, is a localization map of modules at S. Explicitly: multiplication by each s in S on B tensor_A T is an invertible A-linear endomorphism; for every z in B tensor_A T there are t in T and s in S with s z=1 tensor t; and if 1 tensor t_1=1 tensor t_2 then there is s in S with s t_1=s t_2. The scalar localization premise means denominators from S become units, each element of B has a numerator from A and denominator from S, and equality of two images from A is witnessed after multiplying by an element of S.

argument.text: Put T=Q tensor_R J and U=Q tensor_R M_R, and let mu:T -> C be multiplication. The nonzero elements of R form a multiplicative submonoid, and Q is the scalar localization at that submonoid: R embeds in Q, every rational is an integer numerator divided by a nonzero integer denominator (both are in R), all nonzero denominators become units, and equality of two embedded elements is already equality in R. Apply M003 with A=R, B=Q, S=R minus {0}, first to J and also to M_R. In particular every element of T can be written (1/s) tensor c for c in J and nonzero s in R, by its surjectivity clause and multiplication by s^(-1). If mu of this element is zero, then c/s=0 in C and c=0, whence the tensor is zero. Thus mu is injective. The analogous multiplication U -> V is injective by exactly the same numerator argument. Since N003 says J is finitely generated, tensors of its finite generators span T over Q. Thus T is finite dimensional.

produces.statement: mu:T -> C is injective. Every element of T is a tensor (1/s) tensor c for c in J and nonzero s in R. T is finite dimensional over Q. Multiplication U -> V is also injective.

argument.text: Choose m as an R-basis of M_R indexed by I using N002 and N001. M001 with A=R and B=Q makes 1 tensor m_i a Q-basis of U. Apply M004 over Q to this basis. Since card(I)=n by N001, dim_Q U=n.

argument.text: Set r0=dim_Q T, finite by F001. Tensor the coordinate decomposition in N003: explicitly define a Q-linear map T^I -> U by sending an elementary tuple whose i-th component is q tensor c and all others zero to q tensor (c e_i). Its inverse sends q tensor z to the tuple (q tensor coord_i(z))_i, where coord_i is the R-linear inverse-coordinate map in N003. The balancing relations make both maps well-defined, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors and on elementary tuples, hence on all finite sums. Thus U is isomorphic to T^I. Apply M002 over Q, with every factor equal to T. The factors are finite dimensional by F001 and are free because they are vector spaces; hence dim_Q(T^I)=sum_{i in I} r0=n r0. Transport of a basis through the displayed isomorphism preserves its finite cardinality, so M004 and F002 give n=n r0. N001 gives n>0, so r0=1. Combining this with F001 proves the injection and rank-one assertions and says that the image of mu is a one-dimensional rational subspace of C containing J.

produces.statement: dim_Q T=1, mu is injective, and its image is the rational span of J in C. In particular, for any nonzero a in J, every c in J has the form c=q a for some q in Q, nonzero if c is nonzero.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary rational q0 and assume L1: q0!=0. Its signed integer numerator has nonzero absolute value, and its denominator is a positive natural number. Apply M005 to each of these two nonzero natural numbers, setting its q-parameter to p; H001 gives p>=2, hence p!=1. Choose the resulting pairs (alpha0,A0) and (beta0,B0), so abs(num(q0))=p^alpha0 A0, den(q0)=p^beta0 B0, and neither A0 nor B0 is divisible by p. Both remainders are nonzero, since the numerator and denominator are nonzero. Define d0=alpha0-beta0 and let u0 be A0/B0 with the sign of num(q0). Then q0=p^d0 u0. Both u0 and its inverse have denominator not divisible by p, so u0 is a unit of R. Discharge L1 and universally quantify q0. This proves the scalar decomposition for every nonzero rational, allowing either sign of the integer exponent.

produces.statement: For every nonzero q in Q there exist an integer d and a unit u of R such that q=p^d u.

argument.text: Choose nonzero a0 in J and a finite nonempty tuple g of nonzero generators of J, using N003; removing zero entries leaves a generating tuple, and emptiness would force J=0. F003 gives g_j=qg_j a0 with nonzero rationals qg_j. Use F004 to choose qg_j=p^(nu_j)ug_j with integers nu_j and units ug_j in R. The finite nonempty tuple nu has a minimum nu_min. Put b0=p^(nu_min)a0, which is nonzero. For every generator, g_j=p^(nu_j-nu_min)ug_j b0 lies in R b0, because nu_j-nu_min is nonnegative. A generator at the minimum is ug_j b0 with ug_j a unit; therefore b0 belongs to J and that generator generates R b0. It follows in both directions that J=R b0. N003 then gives spanning of M_R by b0 e_i; their independence follows from the complex independence of e in N001 and b0!=0. Thus they are an R-basis, and b=b0 is the required generator and basis scalar. No claim that every submodule of C has rank one was made: the essential rank computation is S003.
